project_context: Research proposal only, not implemented features. Afterlife Lease combines domestic zombie life sim, smooth non-voxel building, crafting and a walkable expanding world. Primary home safe both inbound and outbound; Home mode for everyone and only mode under15. Frontier requires15+, second home and explicit opt-in. Existing Fable proposals cover combat power/tactics/gear/vehicles/defences/death/respawn, zombie style slots/photo consent/social fight posts. Do not redo them; identify missing decisions. Old ART_DIRECTION says cosy macabre diorama and no image textures, but newer premium bodies use gritty PBR high/low files; flag coherence/budget conflict instead of picking a winner. No online launch, age rating, cross-save or new features are verified by these docs. Frontiers consume short decision packets; raw research remains local. No paid APIs or licensed art copying.

sources.verified_excerpt: Official Sims page describes careers, skills, friends, relationships and creative tools.
Official introduction distinguishes Creative and Survival; Survival includes exploration, resource collection, crafting, monsters and experience.
Official properties guide describes customizable high-end apartments, heist planning rooms, arcades and Auto Shop modification bays and garages.
Official guide describes custom Loadouts before matches and different equipment/perk combinations.
Official overview describes story arcs, customizable personal bases, conveniences, Lair Battles and League Halls.
Official docs describe spatial memory accounting and unloading unseen props and terrain; cell memory views aid complex island construction.
Official template catalogs furniture and decoration props from Creative galleries.
Xbox Accessibility Guidelines provide best practices for accessible game development; guidelines do not certify this game.
ESRB guide distinguishes cartoon, fantasy and intense violence and lists category/content descriptors. It is not an assigned rating for our game.
PEGI describes fantasy or non-realistic human-like violence for12, with increasingly realistic-looking violence at16/18. Whole-game assessment still required.
Official Anti-Cheat docs describe authoritative game-server mode using client and server interfaces, and platform-specific limitations.
Steam Cloud stores game files for use across Steam computers. Cross-platform saves need compatible files and Root Overrides; this is not automatically browser/mobile account cross-save.

combat-power.md at f3c7dd289aea3adfb30047d7240879fccbe7eb1d (bounded excerpt): # Combat: power levels and hit tactics — proposal for the lead (owner direction, 2026-11-11)

Status: **proposal, nothing built.** Author: Fable 5.2 ZSM. For Claude Cloud to accept, change or reject; it extends
`docs/DESIGN_OPEN_WORLD.md` §4.7 (combat), §4.8 (raid nights) and §4.8.1 (takeovers) and would become workboard rows
under W-141 / W-144 / W-147.

## 1. Owner direction (verbatim, 2026-11-11 evening)

> "because we are going to have zombies able to fight and try to raid and take over when somebody has more than one
> home we need to have power levels and hit tractics and so on"

> "we need to have zombies can die and respawn and all that type of thing"

> "think of how call of duty works with power and attacks it means that you will have weapons and things and maybe
> like GTA that you can take cars and things and buy and build defences systems but your main home is like safe
> place"

Reading (mine): fights, raids and takeovers of second homes need (a) a number that says how strong a zombie or a crew
is, (b) choices in a fight that matter, so the stronger side does not simply win, and (c) zombies that can be killed
in a fight and come back (respawn), as in other online games.

## 2. What already constrains this

- Raids and takeovers are opt-in, loss is bounded, primary homes are never taken (§4.8, §4.8.1; OW-13, OW-14, OW-19).
- The first build of both is **asynchronous with exact replay**: the fight must be a deterministic function of the
  recorded commands and a seed (OW-15). No float drift, no wall-clock, no unseeded randomness.
- Rating stays E10+ until the owner decides O-1: hits are comic (stuffing, dust, stars, limbs pop off and go back).
- Real money must stay out of chance outcomes (D-006) and purchased items are never at risk.

## 3. Proposal

### 3.1 Power level (one visible number per zombie, one per crew)

- **Zombie power** = `round(10 × (1 + level))` shaped by four combat stats, each 0-10, earned in play:
  | Stat | Raised by (existing systems) | Effect |
  |---|---|---|
  | Might | exercise job, moving furniture, `punch` practice | hit damage |
  | Grit | sleep, meals, low `feral` time | hit points, limb-loss resistance |
  | Reach | intact limbs (a missing arm lowers it), walking distance | who strikes first, grab range |
  | Cunning | study job, chess, lookout duty | tactic slots (§3.2), scouting detail |
- `level` = floor of the mean of the four stats. Power is shown on the zombie card and summed (with diminishing
  returns: 100 %, 80 %, 60 %, 50 % …) into **crew power**, so six weak zombies do not equal one strong crew.
- **Matchmaking band.** A raid or takeover attempt is allowed only when attacker crew power is within a band of the
  defender's posted defence power (start: 0.7× to 1.5×). Outside the band the attempt is refused with the reason
  shown. This is what stops a high-level crew farming new players.
- **Defence power** of a home = defenders present + guard pets + alarms / locks / lights (W-142), posted on the
  home's contested listing so an attacker sees the number before committing.

### 3.2 Hit tactics (the choices)

A fight is a sequence of **exchanges**. Each side picks one tactic per exchange; picks are simultaneous.

| Tactic | Beats | Loses to | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| Swing (heavy hit) | Grab | Brace | full Might damage |
| Grab (hold / shove) | Brace | Swing | moves the target, sets up a crew-mate |
| Brace (guard) | Swing | Grab | halves damage taken, returns a little |
| Feint | reads the other side's pick first | costs the exchange if it reads nothing useful | needs Cunning ≥ 4 |

- Winning the pick multiplies that exchange's result (start: ×1.5), losing it divides (÷1.5), a tie plays straight.
  Stats set the size of a hit; tactics set who gets it. A crew 30 % weaker that reads well can win.
- **Positions:** front (takes hits first), flank (bonus when the target is Grabbed), back (lookout / carrier, cannot
  be hit until the front falls). Crew roles of §4.8 map onto them: breaker = front, guard = front on defence,
  lookout = back, carrier = back.
- **Limbs:** a lost arm removes Swing or Grab (the player chooses which hand it was), a lost leg forces the back
  position. Limbs come back after the event, as today.
- **Defender AI for the asynchronous build:** the owner saves a **defence plan** per home: positions and a tactic
  rule per defender ("Brace until hit twice, then Swing"; "Grab whoever carries"). The replay runs that plan.

### 3.3 Death and respawn

- A zombie at 0 hit points **dies** (they are zombies: it is a comic collapse into a heap, per §4.7 `comic`).
- **Respawn:** it rises again at its household's **respawn point** after a timer. Start values: 20 s in an open-world
  scuffle, 60 s in a raid or takeover, and each further death in the same event adds 30 s. The respawn point is the
  household's coffin / grave marker on the **primary home** lot (always safe ground, §4.8); a crew attacking away
  from home may place one **field marker**

topics.name: Opt-in raids, base defence and live authority

Focus on latency validation, movement/hit authority, reconnect, bot collusion, rate limits and replay trust. Do not assume kernel anti-cheat works in browser or protects the economy.

Status: **proposal, nothing built.** Author: Fable 5.2 ZSM (W-152 follow-up). For Claude Cloud to accept, change or
reject. Companion to `combat-power.md`.

## 1. Owner direction (2026-11-11)

> "I want people to be able to build out zombies like DCUO ... add things like bite marks and other things like
> exposed brains"

> "did you review and get all the ways that dcuo does their charicter builds and how they do there styles"

> "what if on a paid version we can allow people to have their image uploaded and added as their own zombie
> charicter ... that tripo grant will come in and we can use that to make people part of the game"

> "can we have a social media style like in a feed if somebody is getting attacked or home is taken it comes up
> like a media post"

## 2. What DC Universe Online does (reviewed 2026-11-11; mechanics only, nothing of theirs is to be copied)

Sources: the official site and its guides, the community wiki, one official-forum thread. Full notes with links are
in the seat's research report; the points that matter here:

- **Look is separate from stats.** Wearing an item once adds its look to the character's collection; any collected
  look can then be shown whatever is actually worn. A slot can be held so new gear does not change the look.
- **A fixed list of slots:** head, face, hair, shoulders, chest, back, hands, waist, legs, feet, skin, emblem, aura,
  accessory, weapon looks. Aura had to be split out of Accessory years later.
- **A small palette:** four colours per character; most items expose three colour channels that draw from it.
  Materials override an item's surface; "chroma" packs are materials with preset colours.
- **Whole-body skins** (undead, mummy, rock, chrome ...) replace the body surface. I found **no** modular wound
  parts there: decay is one skin swap, so it cannot be mixed.
- **Saved builds** ("armories"): a named imprint of look plus loadout, several per character, quick to swap.
- **Body types** are cosmetic (18 variants); personality changes stance and emotes only.
- **Money:** looks are earned in play, sold directly, and sold through random capsules. Completing look sets feeds
  feats that give skill points, so paid random cosmetics touch power. That is the loudest complaint players make.

## 3. Proposal: the Zombie Builder

### 3.1 Slots (fixed, short, all on the shared 22-bone rig)

| Group | Slots |
|---|---|
| Body | **Base body** (Classic, a cast body, a premium body, a photo body §4) · **Rot stage** (surface: fresh, grey, mossy, dried; ties to W-033) |
| Wounds (new; one per region) | Head · Face · Torso front · Torso back · Arm L · Arm R · Leg L · Leg R |
| Dress | Hair / headwear · Top · Bottom · Feet · Hands · Back · Accessory |
| Finish | Palette (4 colours) · Aura (flies, fog, glow) |

- **Wound parts are region swaps.** Each part declares the body region it replaces and supplies the mesh for it,
  weighted to the same bones, so it needs no new animation: exposed brain replaces the skull cap; a bite replaces a
  patch of forearm; missing flesh shows bone under it. Three layers that mix freely: rot stage (surface), wound
  decals (bites, stitches, scratches), wound parts (missing flesh, exposed brain, open ribs).
- **Conflicts are data, with a safe fallback:** a hat with an exposed brain, a sleeve over a missing forearm. A
  combination with no rule falls back to the plain region, never to a broken body.
- **Colour:** tint masks per item, three channels from the 4-colour palette. Per-item overrides are stored, so
  changing the palette does not reset them (a known flaw in the reference game).
- **Saved looks** are first-class: name, thumbnail, several per zombie, separate from any fight loadout. A look
  that cannot be saved is refused when it is made, not when it is loaded.
- **Earned once, owned on the account.** Collecting a part unlocks its look for every zombie in the household.
- **Looks never touch power** (CB-2 of `combat-power.md`): no stats, no feats that give stats, and every body
  fights with the same hit volumes. No random paid capsules; parts are earned in play or sold directly at a shown
  price.
- **Rating:** exposed brains and open ribs are comic at E10+ only if drawn as stuffing, cartoon bone and green goo.
  Realistic wounds are part of decision O-1.

### 3.2 What it needs

- **Art (my lane):** the premium bodies were generated as one mesh each; wound parts need the body cut into the
  eight regions once per base body, then parts authored in Blender on the same skeleton. The Classic and the cast
  kit need the same region cut to share parts. First set proposed: bite (arm), stitched scar (face), exposed brain
  (head), open ribs (torso), bone forearm (arm), chewed calf (leg).
- **Runtime:** a region-hide mask per body, part attach on the skinned mesh, tint masks; draw-call budget per zombie
  rises from 1 to a bounded few (to be meas

Status: **proposal, nothing built.** Author: Fable 5.2 ZSM. For Claude Cloud to accept, change or reject; it extends
`docs/DESIGN_OPEN_WORLD.md` §4.7 (combat), §4.8 (raid nights) and §4.8.1 (takeovers) and would become workboard rows
under W-141 / W-144 / W-147.

## 1. Owner direction (verbatim, 2026-11-11 evening)

> "because we are going to have zombies able to fight and try to raid and take over when somebody has more than one
> home we need to have power levels and hit tractics and so on"

> "we need to have zombies can die and respawn and all that type of thing"

> "think of how call of duty works with power and attacks it means that you will have weapons and things and maybe
> like GTA that you can take cars and things and buy and build defences systems but your main home is like safe
> place"

Reading (mine): fights, raids and takeovers of second homes need (a) a number that says how strong a zombie or a crew
is, (b) choices in a fight that matter, so the stronger side does not simply win, and (c) zombies that can be killed
in a fight and come back (respawn), as in other online games.

## 2. What already constrains this

- Raids and takeovers are opt-in, loss is bounded, primary homes are never taken (§4.8, §4.8.1; OW-13, OW-14, OW-19).
- The first build of both is **asynchronous with exact replay**: the fight must be a deterministic function of the
  recorded commands and a seed (OW-15). No float drift, no wall-clock, no unseeded randomness.
- Rating stays E10+ until the owner decides O-1: hits are comic (stuffing, dust, stars, limbs pop off and go back).
- Real money must stay out of chance outcomes (D-006) and purchased items are never at risk.

## 3. Proposal

### 3.1 Power level (one visible number per zombie, one per crew)

- **Zombie power** = `round(10 × (1 + level))` shaped by four combat stats, each 0-10, earned in play:
  | Stat | Raised by (existing systems) | Effect |
  |---|---|---|
  | Might | exercise job, moving furniture, `punch` practice | hit damage |
  | Grit | sleep, meals, low `feral` time | hit points, limb-loss resistance |
  | Reach | intact limbs (a missing arm lowers it), walking distance | who strikes first, grab range |
  | Cunning | study job, chess, lookout duty | tactic slots (§3.2), scouting detail |
- `level` = floor of the mean of the four stats. Power is shown on the zombie card and summed (with diminishing
  returns: 100 %, 80 %, 60 %, 50 % …) into **crew power**, so six weak zombies do not equal one strong crew.
- **Matchmaking band.** A raid or takeover attempt is allowed only when attacker crew power is within a band of the
  defender's posted defence power (start: 0.7× to 1.5×). Outside the band the attempt is refused with the reason
  shown. This is what stops a high-level crew farming new players.
- **Defence power** of a home = defenders present + guard pets + alarms / locks / lights (W-142), posted on the
  home's contested listing so an attacker sees the number before committing.

### 3.2 Hit tactics (the choices)

A fight is a sequence of **exchanges**. Each side picks one tactic per exchange; picks are simultaneous.

| Tactic | Beats | Loses to | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| Swing (heavy hit) | Grab | Brace | full Might damage |
| Grab (hold / shove) | Brace | Swing | moves the target, sets up a crew-mate |
| Brace (guard) | Swing | Grab | halves damage taken, returns a little |
| Feint | reads the other side's pick first | costs the exchange if it reads nothing useful | needs Cunning ≥ 4 |

- Winning the pick multiplies that exchange's result (start: ×1.5), losing it divides (÷1.5), a tie plays straight.
  Stats set the size of a hit; tactics set who gets it. A crew 30 % weaker that reads well can win.
- **Positions:** front (takes hits first), flank (bonus when the target is Grabbed), back (lookout / carrier, cannot
  be hit until the front falls). Crew roles of §4.8 map onto them: breaker = front, guard = front on defence,
  lookout = back, carrier = back.
- **Limbs:** a lost arm removes Swing or Grab (the player chooses which hand it was), a lost leg forces the back
  position. Limbs come back after the event, as today.
- **Defender AI for the asynchronous build:** the owner saves a **defence plan** per home: positions and a tactic
  rule per defender ("Brace until hit twice, then Swing"; "Grab whoever carries"). The replay runs that plan.

### 3.3 Death and respawn

- A zombie at 0 hit points **dies** (they are zombies: it is a comic collapse into a heap, per §4.7 `comic`).
- **Respawn:** it rises again at its household's **respawn point** after a timer. Start values: 20 s in an open-world
  scuffle, 60 s in a raid or takeover, and each further death in the same event adds 30 s. The respawn point is the
  household's coffin / grave marker on the **primary home** lot (always safe ground, §4.8); a crew attacking away
  from home may place one **field marker**

ART_DIRECTION.md at f3c7dd289aea3adfb30047d7240879fccbe7eb1d (bounded excerpt): # Art Direction — "Cosy Macabre Diorama"

**One-liner:** a warm, toy-like dollhouse of the undead — soft bevelled shapes, chunky proportions, moody lighting,
funny-gross details. Think hand-painted miniature set, not horror realism. Readable at a zoomed-out isometric-ish camera.

## Palette (sRGB hex)
- **Night plum** `#1d1726` (UI base, sky at night) · **Grave slate** `#2b2f3a` · **Moss** `#6f8f5e` · **Toxic glow** `#9fe870` (accents, selection wisp)
- **Bone** `#e8e0c8` · **Parchment** `#d9cfb8` · **Rust** `#a5532f` · **Blood wine** `#6e2a35` · **Candle** `#ffb35a` · **Cryo** `#7fe0ff`
- Skin tones: see `SKIN_TONES` in `src/shared/appearance.ts` (desaturated greens, greys, lilacs, parchments).
- Avoid pure black/white; keep saturation moderate except emissive accents (screens, candles, cryo, toxic glow).

## Shapes & materials
- Everything bevelled (bevel width 0.01–0.03 m, 2 segments) with smooth/auto-smooth shading; slightly crooked/asymmetric
  (rotate parts 1–4°, uneven legs, sagging cushions). Chunky proportions (+15% thickness vs realistic).
- Materials: Principled BSDF, roughness 0.55–0.9, metallic only for chrome/steel (0.6–0.9). Flat colours + optional vertex-colour
  ambient occlusion. No image textures in GLBs (keeps assets tiny and stylised). Emissive materials for screens/flames/glows
  (strength 2–6) — the renderer's bloom picks them up.
- Recolourable primary material MUST be named `Paint`. Glass named `Glass` (alpha ~0.35). Emissive parts as their own nodes
  named by `DynamicPart` (see `src/shared/catalog.ts`).
- Poly budget: furniture 300–3,000 tris; large items ≤ 6,000; character ≤ 14,000 tris total with all variants hidden-but-present (≈4k visible per zombie, ≤ ~28 draw calls).

## Characters (zombies)
- Stylised chibi-adjacent proportions: head ~1/4.5 of height, big expressive eyes (droopy lids), small nose, wide thin mouth,
  slightly hunched posture, long arms. Visible stitch seams (dark thread crosses) when `stitches` on. Skin tinted by tone,
  shifting toward a sicklier green-grey with darker blotches as decay rises.
- Clothing reads as worn and old-fashioned: frayed hems, patches, a missing button.
- Animation feel: zombies are slow and floppy but *earnest* — they do mundane things carefully. Walk = shuffling, slight drag
  of one foot, arms half-raised; idle = gentle sway, occasional head tilt/twitch; happy = bouncy shoulders; sad = slump.
  Never menacing toward the player; comedic timing.

## Lighting & world
- Day: soft warm-grey overcast sun, long shadows, light fog `#9aa39a`. Dusk: lilac/orange. Night: deep blue-plum ambient with
  a big pale moon, warm interior lamps, emissive windows glowing at night. Full-moon nights tint everything slightly green.
- Ground: muted moss grass with subtle noise, cracked sidewalk, dark road with faded lines, neighbouring crooked houses,
  dead trees and an iron fence fading into fog.
- Post: ACES tonemapping, subtle bloom on emissives, gentle vignette. No heavy grain/chromatic aberration.
- **Miniature-set look (signature, High/Ultra; `src/render/core/diorama.ts`):** tilt-shift focus keeps the middle
  60 % of the view sharp and softens the top and bottom edges (max 4.5 px at 720p, scaled with view height), so the
  lot reads as a tiny model on a table. Shadows lean plum, highlights lean candle. It switches off in build/buy mode,
  the focus line stays centred under Reduce motion, and players can turn it off (Settings → Miniature focus).

## UI
- "Gothic stationery": dark plum glass panels (`rgba(29,23,38,0.86)` + 1px bone border at 15% opacity), bone-white text,
  toxic-green and candle-orange accents, 10–14px rounded corners, soft drop shadows. Display font: a characterful serif
  (bundled offline: system serif fallback stack `"Iowan Old Style","Palatino Linotype",Palatino,Georgia,serif`);
  UI font: system sans stack. Icons: custom inline SVG (rounded strokes 1.75px).
- Need bars colour ramp: low = candle orange `#ff9a4a`, high = teal `#55d6be` (colourblind-safe); colourblind mode adds hatching.
- Motion: 120–200ms ease-out panel transitions; respect `reduceMotion`.
